narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language

scenes.title: Cold open
narration: The Dance That Slowed Down the World
This is Boston. Late 19th to early 20th century.

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The Boston originated in the United States around 1880.
It gained significant popularity in European salons, particularly in Paris and London, between 1895 and 1907.
It is considered a precursor to the modern Slow Waltz, which developed in England by 1920.
on_screen: Map: United States · Global
Image — MISSING

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The Boston served as a relaxing, elegant alternative to more vigorous dances like the polka.
It was valued for its ease of learning and its ability to provide a sophisticated, intimate experience for couples.
Today it is a historical tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is performed in a closed couple position.
Dancers execute long, gliding steps, either moving in a straight line or turning.
The rhythm is a slow 3/4 time, with a characteristic emphasis on the first beat of the measure.
Watch for Boston Dip.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (OXjyeKwXp3o)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Straight lines or turning
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music is written in a slow 3/4 time, often featuring popular melodies of the era.
Key characteristics include a consistent emphasis on the first beat, sometimes contrasted with four-beat counter-rhythms.
The pulse is 3/4.
A slow, flowing 3/4 time signature characterized by a strong emphasis on the first beat, often featuring melodic lines that contrast with the steady, rhythmic pulse.
on_screen: Instrument names on screen as each is mentioned

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: The dance was typically performed in formal ballroom settings, such as salons.
It was associated with the elegant social life of the late 19th and early 20th centuries, often performed in spaces with carpets and heavy drapery.
on_screen: Images — MISSING
Reconstruction imagery allowed only from the costume notes, labelled 'reconstruction'

scenes.title: The people
narration: Variations include the Long Boston (Philadelphia Boston), Walking Boston, One-Step, Short Boston, Dip Boston, Spanish Boston, French Boston, Herring Bone Boston, English Boston (Three-Step), Four-Step, Five-Step, Seven-Step, Double Boston (Cross Boston), Triple Boston, Triple Double Boston, and Russian Boston.
The Boston is a type of ballroom dance that influenced the development of the modern Slow Waltz.
